lesson_title: The 10 Phantom Learners in the School Hall
hook_text: 24 netball players + 18 tennis players = 42. But only 32 kids are standing in the rings. Who are the 10 phantoms?
clip_script: The sports organiser needs one number: how many learners play at least one of the two sports? A helper tries the obvious route: read the netball register — 24 names — and the tennis register — 18 names — and add them: 42. But look down at the floor: only 32 learners are standing inside rope. Who are the 10 phantoms? Walk to the lens and study the ten learners standing there. Every one of them appears on BOTH registers — once as a netball player, once as a tennis player. The addition counted their bodies twice. They are not two people each; they are one person holding two memberships. The repair takes exactly one move: subtract the overlap once. Forty-two minus 10 is 32.
visual_style: Top-down view of a school hall floor with two glowing rope rings crossing, stick figures walking into regions, ghostly duplicate figures appearing in the lens and then dissolving as the subtraction lands.
pacing: Build the miscount quickly, freeze on 42 vs 32, slow reveal at the lens, snap resolution with the single subtraction.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master Venn diagrams and the addition rule.
